title: Socratic checklist — search & retrieval (检索)
rationale: Before executing database searches, the agent audits the strategy itself. Answers are recorded; the gate checks completeness. Sources are chapter/item-level references, not page numbers.

items.question: Is the search strategy derived from the certificate's concepts, controlled vocabulary, and free-text terms with a documented derivation, not pasted from another database?
items.rationale: Concept drift between question and query silently truncates the evidence base.
items.source: Cochrane Handbook v6 Ch.4 (searching for and selecting studies); PRISMA-S item 4 (full search strategy)
items.answer_format: concept -> term table + per-database translation log

items.question: Was the strategy validated with a known-item test (a set of studies that must be retrieved) and a recall check before full execution?
items.rationale: A strategy that cannot retrieve known relevant studies has unknown recall.
items.source: Cochrane Handbook v6 Ch.4; PRISMA-S item 7 (prior work)
items.answer_format: known-item list + retrieved/missed counts + revision log

items.question: Are validated filters (RCT, human, date) applied where appropriate, with the filter version recorded?
items.rationale: Filter versioning is required for reproducibility; unversioned filters drift silently.
items.source: Cochrane Handbook v6 Ch.4 (search filters); PRISMA-S item 6 (limits and restrictions)
items.answer_format: filter names + versions + the databases they were applied to

items.question: Is every source-specific strategy stored exactly as run, with the run date, the raw export, and a query hash?
items.rationale: Reproducibility of the search is a PRISMA requirement and the basis of the living-update diff.
items.source: PRISMA-S items 3-5 (database, date, full strategy); MetaWingman search audit norm
items.answer_format: file map: strategy text / run date / export / hash per database

items.question: Are registries, preprint servers, and grey sources covered per the protocol, with their coverage explicitly recorded?
items.rationale: Unpublished and ongoing studies are required for a complete evidence map and for reporting-bias assessment.
items.source: Cochrane Handbook v6 Ch.4; PRISMA-S items 8-12 (registers, websites, citation searching, contact)
items.answer_format: sources searched + counts + explicit 'not searched' list with reason

items.question: Is the deduplication method (fuzzy keys, thresholds) fixed and audited so the PRISMA flow counts can be reproduced?
items.rationale: Dedup errors propagate into every later stage count.
items.source: PRISMA 2020 item 3 (records identified via databases/registers); MECIR
items.answer_format: dedup tool + threshold + pre/post counts + merge log

items.question: Does the search date boundary match the certificate's time window and the living-update cadence?
items.rationale: The novelty claim depends on the exact window; mismatch invalidates the gap analysis.
items.source: Cochrane Handbook v6 Ch.4 (updating searches); PRISMA-S item 8
items.answer_format: start/end dates + cadence + overlap with nearest prior review's last search

items.question: Were zero-hit or anomalous-result sources investigated rather than silently accepted?
items.rationale: Zero hits usually mean query error, not empty evidence.
items.answer_format: per-source hit counts + investigation note for anomalies

items.question: Is the full search strategy included verbatim in the supplement so a reviewer can re-run it line by line?
items.rationale: Summaries of searches are not reproducible; verbatim strategy text is the PRISMA-S default.
items.answer_format: supplement file path with verbatim strategies for every database

items.question: Which single query revision between protocol and execution would most change the review's evidence base?
items.rationale: Naming the load-bearing revision turns search drift into a documented, testable decision.
